Plot a Raster Grid (GeoTIFF/NetCDF) as a Publication-Ready Map

Source: R/sus_grid_plot.R
sus_grid_plot.Rd

sus_grid_plot() renders a raster surface – a SpatRaster, a single GeoTIFF/NetCDF file path, or the named vector of cached file paths returned by the sus_grid_*() family (e.g. sus_grid_chirps(), sus_grid_era5(), sus_grid_pdsi(), sus_grid_pollution_ghap(), sus_grid_pollution_merra2()) when called with municipalities = NULL or raster_area != FALSE – as a ggplot2 map, following the same publication style used across the other sus_*_plot_*() functions.

Use it after any sus_grid_*() call that returns rasters/paths (stage 8, gridded climate/environment) to inspect a surface before aggregating it. Large rasters are automatically downsampled for plotting (see max_cells).

Usage

sus_grid_plot(
  x,
  layer = 1,
  max_layers = 12,
  municipalities = NULL,
  state_borders = TRUE,
  diverging = FALSE,
  palette = "viridis",
  name = NULL,
  max_cells = 5e+05,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  base_size = 11,
  interactive = FALSE,
  use_cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = "~/.climasus4r_cache/spatial",
  lang = "pt",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A terra::SpatRaster; a single file path ("file.tif", "file.tif.gz", "file.nc"); or a (named) character vector of file paths, as returned by sus_grid_*() with municipalities = NULL (layers are stacked and named by the vector names). Any other class errors; an empty vector errors; missing files error.

layer

Single layer selector, or "all". Forms: integer index (1, 3), layer name ("2022-01-01"; must match names(x)), or "all" to facet every layer (capped at max_layers). Default 1. A single value only (vectors such as 1:3 are not supported); index outside 1:nlyr or unknown name errors.

max_layers

Positive integer. Maximum layers drawn when layer = "all"; the first max_layers are kept and a warning is printed. Default 12.

municipalities

An sf polygon object (e.g. rows from geobr::read_municipality() or a state polygon) or NULL (default). When supplied, the raster is reprojected-to-match, cropped and masked to it (cells outside become NA and are not drawn) and its boundary is overlaid. NULL = full raster extent.

state_borders

Logical scalar. Overlay Brazilian state boundaries (needs geobr and sf, cached on disk; if unavailable a warning is issued and borders are omitted). Default TRUE.

diverging

Logical scalar. If TRUE, use a blue-white-red scale centered on 0 with symmetric limits (for anomalies/indices such as PDSI) and ignore palette. Default FALSE.

palette

Character scalar. Sequential palette used when diverging = FALSE: "viridis" (default), "plasma", "magma", "inferno", "cividis", or any RColorBrewer::brewer.pal() palette name (e.g. "YlOrRd", "Blues"). Unknown names fall back to "YlOrRd" with a warning.

name

Character scalar or NULL (default). Legend title; NULL uses the (first) layer name.

max_cells

Numeric scalar. If the number of cells x layers exceeds this, the raster is regularly subsampled before plotting. Default 500000.

title

Character scalar or NULL (default, built-in title in lang).

subtitle

Character scalar or NULL (default, auto-generated from the layer name / number of layers).

caption

Character scalar or NULL (default, a generic climasus4r line).

base_size

Numeric scalar. Base font size for ggplot2::theme_void(). Default 11.

interactive

Logical scalar. If TRUE, return plotly::ggplotly() of the map (requires plotly). Default FALSE.

use_cache

Logical scalar. Cache the downloaded state boundaries on disk. Default TRUE.

cache_dir

Character scalar. Directory of the boundary cache. Default "~/.climasus4r_cache/spatial".

lang

Character scalar. Message and label language: "pt" (default), "en" or "es" (validated with match.arg(); other values error).

verbose

Logical scalar. Print progress messages. Default TRUE.

Value

A ggplot object (a raster layer in lon/lat with optional state and municipality outlines; faceted by layer when layer = "all"), or a plotly object when interactive = TRUE. Not a climasus_df; sus_meta is not involved.

See also

sus_grid_chirps(), sus_grid_era5(), sus_grid_pdsi(), sus_grid_pollution_ghap(), sus_grid_pollution_merra2(), sus_grid_join(), sus_data_plot_aggregate_map()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(climasus4r)

# From a raster returned in memory
r <- sus_grid_chirps(resolution = "annual", years = 2022,
                      raster_area = TRUE)
sus_grid_plot(r, lang = "pt")

# From cached GeoTIFF paths, faceting every month
paths <- sus_grid_chirps(resolution = "monthly", years = 2022)
sus_grid_plot(paths, layer = "all", lang = "en")

# Anomaly-style raster with a diverging palette
sus_grid_plot(r, diverging = TRUE, name = "Anomaly (mm)")
} # }
